paragraphs.sourceText: In this section you will hear a mini-lecture. You will hear the mini-lecture ONCE ONLY. While listening to the mini-lecture, complete the gap-filling task on ANSWER SHEET ONE and write NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS for each gap. Make sure what you fill in is both grammatically and semantically acceptable. You may use the blank sheet for note-taking.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在本节中，您将听到一个小型讲座。您只会听到一次迷你讲座。听迷你讲座时，完成第一张答题卡上的填空任务，并为每个空白写不超过三个单词。确保您填写的内容在语法和语义上都是可接受的。您可以使用空白纸做笔记。

paragraphs.sourceText: You have THIRTY seconds to preview the gap-filling task.
paragraphs.translationZh: 您有三十秒的时间来预览填补空白的任务。

paragraphs.sourceText: Now, listen to the mini-lecture. When it is over, you will be given THREE minutes to check your work.
paragraphs.translationZh: 现在，请听小讲座。结束后，您将有三分钟时间检查您的工作。

paragraphs.sourceText: In this section you will hear ONE interviews. The interview will be divided into TWO parts. At the end of each part, five questions will be asked about what was said. Both the interview and the questions will be read ONCE ONLY. After each question there will be a ten-second pause. During the pause, you should read the four choices of A, B, C and D, and mark the best answer to each question on ANSWER SHEET TWO.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在本节中，您将听到一次采访。采访将分为两部分。在每个部分的最后，将针对所讲内容提出五个问题。采访和问题都只会阅读一次。每个问题后都会有十秒钟的停顿。暂停期间，您应该阅读 A、B、C、D 四个选项，并在第二张答题卡上标记每个问题的最佳答案。

paragraphs.sourceText: You have THIRTY seconds to preview the choices.
paragraphs.translationZh: 您有三十秒的时间来预览选项。

paragraphs.sourceText: Now, listen to Part One of the interview. Questions 1 to 5 are based on Part One of the interview.
paragraphs.translationZh: 现在，请听采访的第一部分。问题 1 至 5 基于采访的第一部分。

paragraphs.sourceText: Now, listen to Part Two of the interview. Questions 6 to 10 are based on Part Two of the interview.
paragraphs.translationZh: 现在，请听采访的第二部分。问题 6 至 10 基于采访的第二部分。

paragraphs.sourceText: In this section there are three passages followed by fourteen multiple choice questions. For each multiple choice question, there are four suggested answers marked A, B, C and D. Choose the one that you think is the best answer and mark your answers on ANSWER SHEET TWO.
paragraphs.translationZh: 本节由三篇文章组成，后面是十四道多项选择题。对于每个多项选择题，有四个建议答案，标记为 A、B、C 和 D。选择您认为最佳答案的一个，并将您的答案标记在答题表二上。

paragraphs.sourceText: (1) A new study from researchers uncovers the kinds of infrastructure improvements that would make the biggest difference in increasing the number of electric cars on the road, a key step toward reducing greenhouse gas emissions from transportation.
paragraphs.translationZh: (1) 研究人员的一项新研究揭示了哪些基础设施改进能够对增加道路上的电动汽车数量产生最大的影响，这是减少交通运输温室气体排放的关键一步。

paragraphs.sourceText: (2) The researchers found that installing charging stations on residential streets, rather than just in central locations such as shopping malls, could have an outsized benefit. They also found that adding on high-speed charging stations along highways and making supplementary vehicles more easily available to people who need to travel beyond the single-charge range of their electric vehicles could greatly increase the vehicle electrification potential.
paragraphs.translationZh: (2) 研究人员发现，在住宅区街道上安装充电站，而不仅仅是在购物中心等中心位置，可能会带来巨大的好处。他们还发现，在高速公路沿线增加高速充电站，并使需要超出电动汽车单次充电范围的人们更容易获得补充车辆，可以大大增加车辆电气化的潜力。

paragraphs.sourceText: (3) The findings are reported in Nature Energy, in a paper by associate professor of energy studies Jessika Trancik, graduate student Wei Wei, etc.
paragraphs.translationZh: (3) 能源研究副教授 Jessika Trancik 和研究生 Wei Wei 等在 Nature Energy 上发表论文。

paragraphs.sourceText: (4) The researchers developed a new methodology to identify charging solutions that would conveniently fit into people’s daily activities. They used data collected from GPS tracking devices in cars, as well as survey results about people’s daily driving habits and needs, including detailed data from local areas and more general data from the country as a whole. Greatly increasing the penetration of electric cars into the personal vehicle fleet is a central feature of climate mitigation policies at local and national levels, Trancik says. A goal of this study was “to better understand how to make these plans for rapid vehicle electrification a reality,” she adds.
paragraphs.translationZh: (4) 研究人员开发了一种新方法来确定能够方便地适应人们日常活动的充电解决方案。他们使用了从汽车 GPS 跟踪设备收集的数据，以及有关人们日常驾驶习惯和需求的调查结果，包括来自当地的详细数据和来自整个国家的更一般的数据。特兰西克表示，大幅提高电动汽车在个人车队中的渗透率是地方和国家层面气候减缓政策的核心特征。她补充道，这项研究的目标是“更好地了解如何使这些快速车辆电气化计划成为现实”。

paragraphs.sourceText: (5) In deciding how to prioritize different kinds of improvements in vehicle charging infrastructure, she says, “the approach that we took methodologically was to emphasize building a better understanding of people’s detailed energy consuming behavior, throughout the day and year.”
paragraphs.translationZh: (5) 在决定如何优先考虑车辆充电基础设施的不同类型的改进时，她说，“我们在方法上采取的方法是强调更好地了解人们全天和全年的详细能源消耗行为。”

paragraphs.sourceText: (6) To do that, “we examine how different people are moving from location to location throughout the day, and where they are stopping,” she says. “And from there we’re able to look at when and where they would be able to charge without interrupting their daily travel activities.”
paragraphs.translationZh: (6) 为此，“我们研究了不同的人如何在一天中从一个地点移动到另一个地点，以及他们在哪里停留，”她说。 “从那里我们可以了解他们何时何地可以充电，而不会中断他们的日常旅行活动。”

paragraphs.sourceText: (7) The team looked at both regular daily activities and the variations that occur over the course of a year. “The longitudinal view is important for capturing the different kinds of trips that a driver makes over time, so that we can determine the kinds of charging infrastructure needed to support vehicle electrification,” Wei says.
paragraphs.translationZh: (7) 研究小组观察了日常活动和一年中发生的变化。 “纵向视图对于捕捉驾驶员随时间的不同类型的出行非常重要，这样我们就可以确定支持车辆电气化所需的充电基础设施类型，”魏说。

paragraphs.sourceText: (8) While the vast majority of people’s daily driving needs can be met by the range provided by existing lower-cost electric cars, as Trancik and her colleagues have reported, there are typically a few times when people need to drive much farther. Or, they may need to make more short trips than usual in a day, with little time to stop and recharge. These “high-energy days,” as the researchers call them, when drivers are consuming more than the usual amount of energy for their transportation needs, may only happen a handful of times per year, but they can be the deciding factor in people’s decision making about whether to go electric.
paragraphs.translationZh: (8) 正如 Trancik 和她的同事所报告的那样，虽然绝大多数人的日常驾驶需求可以通过现有的低成本电动汽车提供的里程来满足，但有时人们通常需要行驶更远的距离。或者，他们可能需要在一天内进行比平时更多的短途旅行，几乎没有时间停下来充电。研究人员将这些“高能量日”称为“高能量日”，即驾驶员为了满足交通需求而消耗的能量超过平时的能量，这种情况每年可能只发生几次，但它们可能是人们决定是否使用电动汽车的决定性因素。

paragraphs.sourceText: (9) Even though battery technology is steadily improving and extending the maximum range of electric cars, that alone will not be enough to meet all drivers’ needs and achieve rapid emissions reductions. So, addressing the range issue through infrastructure is essential, Wei says. The highest-capacity batteries tend to be the most expensive, and are not affordable to many, he points out, so getting infrastructure right is also important from an equity perspective.
paragraphs.translationZh: (9) 尽管电池技术正在稳步改进并扩大电动汽车的最大续航里程，但仅凭这一点还不足以满足所有驾驶员的需求并实现快速减排。因此，通过基础设施解决范围问题至关重要，魏说。他指出，最高容量的电池往往是最昂贵的，许多人都买不起，因此从公平的角度来看，建立正确的基础设施也很重要。

paragraphs.sourceText: (10) “There are various ways to incentivize the expansion of such charging infrastructures,” he says. “There’s a role for policymakers at the national level, for example, for incentives to encourage private sector competition in this space, and demonstration sites for testing out, through public-private partnerships, the rapid expansion of the charging infrastructure.” Governments at different levels can also play an important part in driving innovation by businesses, he says, and a number of them have already signaled their support for vehicle electrification.
paragraphs.translationZh: (10) “有多种方法可以激励此类充电基础设施的扩张，”他说。 “例如，国家层面的政策制定者可以发挥激励作用，鼓励私营部门在这一领域的竞争，并通过公私合作建立示范点来测试充电基础设施的快速扩张。”他表示，各级政府也可以在推动企业创新方面发挥重要作用，其中一些政府已经表示支持汽车电气化。

paragraphs.sourceText: (11) Providing easy access to alternative transportation for those high-energy days could also play a role, the study found. Vehicle companies may even find it advantageous to provide or partner with convenient rental services to help drive their electric car sales.
paragraphs.translationZh: (11) 研究发现，在那些精力充沛的日子里提供便捷的替代交通也可能发挥作用。汽车公司甚至可能发现提供或合作提供便利的租赁服务以帮助推动其电动汽车销售是有利的。

paragraphs.sourceText: (12) In their analysis of driving habits, for example, the team found that the impact of either adding highway fast-charging stations or increasing availability of supplementary long-range vehicles for up to four days a year meant that the number of homes that could meet their driving needs with a lower cost electric vehicle increased from 10 percent to 40 percent. This number rose to above 90 percent of households when fast-charging stations, workplace charging, overnight public charging, and up to 10 days of access to supplementary vehicles were all available. Importantly, charging options at residential locations (on or off-street) is key across all of these scenarios.
paragraphs.translationZh: (12) 例如，在对驾驶习惯的分析中，研究小组发现，增加高速公路快速充电站或增加每年长达四天的补充远程车辆的可用性所产生的影响意味着能够使用成本较低的电动汽车满足其驾驶需求的家庭数量从 10% 增加到 40%。当快速充电站、工作场所充电、夜间公共充电以及长达 10 天的补充车辆使用权全部可用时，这一数字上升到 90% 以上的家庭。重要的是，住宅地点（街道内或街外）的充电选项是所有这些场景的关键。

paragraphs.sourceText: (13) The study’s findings highlight the importance of making overnight charging capabilities available to more people. While those who have their own garages or off-street parking can often already easily charge their cars at home, many people do not have that option and use public parking. “It’s really important to provide access — reliable, predictable access — to charging for people, wherever they park for longer periods of time near home, often overnight,” Trancik says.
paragraphs.translationZh: (13) 该研究的结果强调了让更多人获得夜间充电功能的重要性。虽然那些拥有自己的车库或街边停车场的人通常可以轻松地在家中为汽车充电，但许多人没有这种选择，而是使用公共停车场。 “为人们提供充电通道——可靠、可预测的通道——非常重要，无论他们在家附近停放较长时间（通常是过夜），”Trancik 说。

paragraphs.sourceText: (14) That includes locations such as hotels as well as residential neighborhoods, she says. “I think it’s so critical to emphasize these high-impact approaches, such as figuring out ways to do that on public streets, rather than haphazardly putting a charger at the grocery store or at the mall or any other public location.”
paragraphs.translationZh: (14) 她说，这包括酒店和住宅区等地点。 “我认为强调这些高影响力的方法非常重要，例如找出在公共街道上这样做的方法，而不是随意在杂货店、商场或任何其他公共场所放置充电器。”

paragraphs.sourceText: (15) The study should help to provide some guidance to policymakers at all levels who are looking for ways to facilitate the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions, since the transportation sector accounts for about a third of those emissions overall. “If you have limited funds, which you typically always do, then it’s just really important to prioritize,” Trancik says, noting that this study could indicate the areas that could provide the greatest return for those investments.
paragraphs.translationZh: (15) 该研究应有助于为各级政策制定者提供一些指导，帮助他们寻找促进减少温室气体排放的方法，因为交通部门约占温室气体排放总量的三分之一。特兰西克说：“如果你的资金有限（通常情况下你总是这样做），那么确定优先顺序就非常重要。”他指出，这项研究可以指出哪些领域可以为这些投资提供最大的回报。

paragraphs.sourceText: 11. The team’s survey involves all the following EXCEPT ______
paragraphs.translationZh: 11.团队的调查涉及以下所有内容，除了______

paragraphs.sourceText: 12. During high-energy days, people tend to ______
paragraphs.translationZh: 12. 在精力充沛的日子里，人们倾向于______

paragraphs.sourceText: 13. Highest-capacity batteries are NOT the best solution to going electric because they ______
paragraphs.translationZh: 13. 最高容量的电池并不是电动化的最佳解决方案，因为它们 ______

paragraphs.sourceText: 14.What does Para.10 mainly discuss?
paragraphs.translationZh: 14.第10段主要讨论什么？

paragraphs.sourceText: 15.Which of the following is the most advisable for going electric?
paragraphs.translationZh: 15.对于电动化来说，以下哪一项是最可取的？

paragraphs.sourceText: (1) I had been hanging around for a few years with a very party-time crowd, and my life was on a downward slide. I had gotten a Ph.D. and a divorce simultaneously. The fancy academic job never materialized. Soon I was playing flute in a street band, eating donated sandwiches, and spending every night in clubs dancing the night away. In a few years I was living in the mountains in a shack, and none of my friends worked.
paragraphs.translationZh: (1) 我已经和一群热衷于聚会的人混在一起了几年，我的生活一直在走下坡路。我已经获得了博士学位。并同时离婚。这份美妙的学术工作从未实现。很快我就在街头乐队中吹长笛，吃着捐赠的三明治，每天晚上都在俱乐部里跳舞通宵达旦。几年后，我住在山里的一个棚屋里，我的朋友都没有工作。

paragraphs.sourceText: (2) When I saw the ad in the Sunday paper — BRAKEMEN WANTED — I thought of it as a chance to clean up my act and to get away. I felt that by doing work this dangerous, I would have to make a decision to live, to protect myself. I would have to choose to stay alive every day, to hang on to the sides of those freight cars for dear life. The railroad transformed the metaphor of my life. Nine thousand tons moving at sixty miles an hour into the fearful night. I now would ride that image, trying to stay alive within it. I know that later, when I sat behind the moving train in the darkness of the caboose (供列车员休息的车厢), window open and the unknown fragrances of the land filling the space, the blackness of the night was my friend. It felt good to be powerless and carried along by the destiny of that motion. I felt happy and at peace. I was where I belonged.
paragraphs.translationZh: (2) 当我在周日报纸上看到广告——招揽刹车员——我认为这是一个改正错误并逃脱的机会。我觉得从事如此危险的工作，我必须做出决定，要活下去，保护自己。我必须选择每天都活着，为了亲爱的生命而紧紧抓住那些货车的侧面。铁路改变了我生活的隐喻。九千吨货物以每小时六十英里的速度驶入可怕的夜晚。我现在会骑在那个形象上，试图在其中保持活力。我知道，后来，当我坐在行驶的火车后面，在黑暗的车厢里，窗户打开，大地未知的香味充满空间时，夜晚的黑暗就是我的朋友。无力并被这项运动的命运所推动的感觉很好。我感到快乐和平安。我就在我所属的地方。

paragraphs.sourceText: (3) The railroad didn’t believe in lengthy formal training. They offered a two-week class which covered the book of rules, a three-hundred-page document with a dual purpose — to keep trains from running into one another and to prevent any situation in which the company might get sued. Rules of the road which you had to learn were mixed in with rules which you had to ignore in order to get the work done. But you had to know that you were ignoring a rule so that in the winter, when company officials had time to sneak around testing, you could work by the book.
paragraphs.translationZh: (3) 铁路不相信长时间的正规培训。他们提供了为期两周的课程，内容涵盖了规则手册，这是一份三百页的文件，具有双重目的——防止火车相撞，并防止公司可能被起诉的任何情况。你必须学习的道路规则与你为了完成工作而必须忽略的规则混合在一起。但你必须知道你忽略了一条规则，这样在冬天，当公司官员有时间偷偷进行测试时，你就可以照章办事。

paragraphs.sourceText: (4) The rulebook was also in a continuous state of revision. Revisions appeared in the timetable which you carried with you at all times. Further revisions appeared in regular timetable bulletins which were posted at work. Soon your rulebook resembled a scrapbook, with paragraphs crossed out, pages pasted in, and notes on changes which were then crossed out and changed weeks later. It drove you crazy. You always had to be on the lookout for a company official hiding in the bushes while you did your work. This individual would pop out and ask you questions about the latest rule revisions. A notation of failure would then appear in your personal file. These notations were referred to as “Brownies,” named after the official who devised the railroad demerit system. As trainmen were fond of pointing out, however, there was no merit system to go with it.
paragraphs.translationZh: (4)规则手册也处于不断修订的状态。修改出现在您随身携带的时间表中。进一步的修改出现在工作中张贴的定期时间表公告中。很快，你的规则手册就像一本剪贴簿，段落被划掉，页面被粘贴，以及更改注释，然后被划掉并在几周后更改。它让你发疯。当你工作时，你必须时刻留意躲在灌木丛中的公司官员。此人会弹出并询问您有关最新规则修订的问题。然后，失败的注释将出现在您的个人档案中。这些符号被称为“布朗尼蛋糕”，以设计铁路扣分制度的官员的名字命名。然而，正如列车员喜欢指出的那样，没有与之相适应的绩效制度。

paragraphs.sourceText: (5) Out of seventeen student brakemen three of us were women. This was a large percentage, comparatively. The first women had been hired two years before, and they were around to give us advice. The point was to get through the class, and get over the probationary period known as the “derail.” Then you were in the union and a railroader for life. Getting over the derail took sixty days, and if either the crews you worked with or the company officers had a complaint, you were out. At the end of two weeks of classroom instruction, you bought a railroad watch, they gave you switch keys and a two-dollar lantern, and you marked up as extra board brakemen.
paragraphs.translationZh: (5) 在 17 名制动员学员中，我们中的 3 名是女性。相比之下，这个比例很大。第一批女性是在两年前被聘用的，她们随时为我们提供建议。重点是要完成课程，并度过被称为“出轨”的试用期。然后你就加入了工会，成为了终生的铁路工人。克服脱轨需要六十天，如果与你一起工作的工作人员或公司官员提出投诉，你就出局了。两周的课堂教学结束后，你买了一块铁路手表，他们给了你开关钥匙和一个两美元的灯笼，你还被标记为额外的董事会制动员。

paragraphs.sourceText: (6) On the last day of class, they took us down to the freightyard to grapple with the equipment. We practiced getting on and off moving cars, climbing the ladders and cranking down the handbrakes, changing the eighty-five-pound knuckles that joined the cars together, and hand and lantern signals. These signals were the way members of the crew talked to each other, and they were an art form. An old head could practically order a pizza from a half mile away. You would see lights, arcs and circles, stabs of light. It would repeat. You would stand there confused. Finally you would walk down the track and find the foreman in a deep state of disgust.
paragraphs.translationZh: (6) 课程的最后一天，他们带我们到货场去处理设备。我们练习上下移动的汽车、爬上梯子、拉下手刹、更换将汽车连接在一起的八十五磅重的指节，以及手势和灯笼信号。这些信号是船员们相互交谈的方式，它们是一种艺术形式。一个老头几乎可以在半英里外订购披萨。你会看到光、弧线、圆圈、光刺。它会重复。你会困惑地站在那里。最后，你沿着轨道走下去，会发现工头处于深深的厌恶之中。

paragraphs.sourceText: (7) “I told you to hang three cars, let two go to the runaround, one to the main, go through the crossovers, and line behind. Now can’t you read a signal, dummy?”
paragraphs.translationZh: (7) “我告诉过你挂三辆车，让两辆车去绕行处，一辆车去主干道，穿过交叉路口，然后在后面排队。现在你看不到信号了吗，傻瓜？”

paragraphs.sourceText: (8) The day after our practice session, I got into my car and tried to roll the window down. My arms didn’t work. This was my first moment of doubt about being able to do the job. It was hard to get the upper-body strength required to hang on and ride for long distances on the side of cars. Terror at falling beneath the wheels was a big motivator, however. Terror and ridicule. There was a lot of both during the probationary period and the student trips. On student trips we tagged along with a regular crew and tried to learn something. To me, what we were doing made no sense whatsoever. Just getting used to the equipment had me so disorientated that I had no idea where we had gone or how the crew did anything. One of the crew suggested to me that I go to a toy store and look at the model trains, to see how switches work. They say, though, that whatever you start out doing railroading, it gets imprinted, and that’s what you are most comfortable doing from then on. I couldn’t have picked a better place to break in than Watsonville Junction. It was old-time, local-freight, full-crew switching. Kicking cars and passing signs. The basic stuff that you have to learn at first or you never get no matter how long you’re out here.
paragraphs.translationZh: (8) 练习结束的第二天，我钻进车里，试图摇下车窗。我的手臂不能用了。这是我第一次对自己能否胜任这份工作产生怀疑。很难获得在汽车侧面挂住并长途骑行所需的上半身力量。然而，对摔倒在车轮下的恐惧是一个很大的动力。恐怖和嘲笑。见习期间和学生旅行期间都有很多。在学生旅行中，我们跟随普通船员并尝试学习一些东西。对我来说，我们所做的一切毫无意义。刚适应这些设备就让我迷失了方向，我不知道我们去了哪里，也不知道工作人员是如何做事的。一名工作人员建议我去一家玩具店看看火车模型，看看开关是如何工作的。不过，他们说，无论你一开始从事铁路行业，它都会留下烙印，从那时起，这就是你最舒服的事情。我找不到比沃森维尔交汇处更好的闯入地点了。这是老式的本地货运、全员轮换。踢汽车和通过标志。你首先必须学习的基本知识，否则无论你在这里呆多久，你都永远学不到。

paragraphs.sourceText: (1) The storm came on slowly one afternoon. The clouds looked as if they were stumbling along before the wind, frightened. The sea took its cue. It started rising and falling in a manner that made my heart sink. I took in the net. Oh, you should have seen that landscape! What I had seen up till now were mere hillocks of water. These swells were truly mountains. The valleys we found ourselves in were so deep they were gloomy. Their sides were so steep the lifeboat started sliding down them, nearly surfing. The raft was getting exceptionally rough treatment, being pulled out of the water and dragged along bouncing. I deployed both sea anchors fully, at different lengths so that they would not interfere with each other.
paragraphs.translationZh: (1) 一天下午，暴风雨慢慢来了。云彩看起来像是在风前跌跌撞撞地走着，受到了惊吓。大海听从了它的暗示。它开始以一种让我的心沉下去的方式起伏。我把网收了。哦，你真该看看那风景！到目前为止我所看到的只是水丘。这些海浪确实是山脉。我们发现自己身处的山谷是如此之深，以至于阴森森的。它们的侧面非常陡峭，救生艇开始从上面滑下来，几乎是在冲浪。木筏受到了异常粗暴的对待，被拉出水面并弹跳着拖着走。我将两个海锚完全展开，长度不同，这样它们就不会互相干扰。

paragraphs.sourceText: (2) Climbing the giant swells, the boat clung to the sea anchors like a mountain climber to a rope. We would rush up until we reached a snow-white crest in a burst of light and foam and a tipping forward of the lifeboat. The view would be clear for miles around. But the mountain would shift, and the ground beneath us would start sinking in a most stomach-sickening way. In no time we would be sitting once again at the bottom of a dark valley, different from the last but the same, with thousands of tons of water hovering above us and with only our flimsy lightness to save us. The land would move once more, the sea-anchor ropes would snap to tautness, and the roller coaster would start again.
paragraphs.translationZh: (2) 攀登巨浪时，船紧紧抓住海锚，就像登山者紧紧抓住绳索一样。我们会冲上去，直到到达雪白的山顶，伴随着一阵光芒和泡沫，救生艇向前倾斜。方圆几英里的视野都清晰可见。但山会移动，我们脚下的地面会开始以最令人胃痛的方式下沉。很快我们就会再次坐在黑暗的山谷底部，与上次不同但又一样，数千吨的水在我们上方盘旋，只有我们脆弱的轻盈来拯救我们。陆地将再次移动，海锚绳索将拉紧，过山车将再次启动。

paragraphs.sourceText: (3) The sea anchors did their job well — in fact, nearly too well. Every swell at its crest wanted to take us for a tumble, but the anchors, beyond the crest, heaved mightily and pulled us through, but at the expense of pulling the front of the boat down. The result was an explosion of foam and spray at the bow. I was soaked through and through each time.
paragraphs.translationZh: (3) 海锚的工作做得很好——事实上，几乎做得太好了。波峰上的每一次海浪都想把我们卷入水中，但波峰之外的锚却猛烈地抛起，把我们拉了过去，但代价是把船的前部拉下来。结果是船头发生泡沫和水花爆炸。我每次都浑身湿透。

paragraphs.sourceText: (4) Then a swell came up that was particularly intent on taking us along. This time the bow vanished underwater. I was shocked and chilled and scared witless. I barely managed to hold on. The boat was swamped. I heard Richard Parker roar. I felt death was upon us. The only choice left to me was death by water or death by animal. I chose death by animal.
paragraphs.translationZh: (4) 然后，一股巨浪涌来，特别想把我们卷走。这次弓消失在水下。我感到震惊、寒冷、害怕得不知所措。我好不容易才坚持下来。船被淹没了。我听到理查德·帕克的怒吼。我感到死亡就在我们身边。留给我的唯一选择就是被水死或者被动物死。我选择了动物的死亡。

paragraphs.sourceText: (5) While we sank down the back of the swell, I jumped onto the tarpaulin (防水布) and unrolled it towards the stern, closing in Richard Parker. If he protested, I did not hear him. Faster than a sewing machine working a piece of cloth, I hooked down the tarpaulin on both sides of the boat. We were climbing again. The boat was lurching upwards steadily. It was hard to keep my balance. The lifeboat was now covered and the tarpaulin battened (用压条固定) down, except at my end. I squeezed in between the side bench and the tarpaulin and pulled the remaining tarpaulin over my head. I did not have much space. Between bench and gunnel (船舷边缘) there was twelve inches, and the side benches were only one and a half feet wide. But I was not so foolhardy, even in the face of death, as to move onto the floor of the boat. There were four hooks left to catch. I slipped a hand through the opening and worked the rope. With each hook done, it was getting harder to get the next. I managed two. Two hooks left. The boat was rushing upwards in a smooth and unceasing motion. The incline was over thirty degrees. I could feel myself being pulled down towards the stern. Twisting my hand frantically, I succeeded in catching one more hook with the rope. It was the best I could do. This was not a job meant to be done from the inside of the lifeboat but from the outside. I pulled hard on the rope, something made easier by the fact that holding on to it was preventing me from sliding down the length of the boat. The boat swiftly passed a forty-five-degree incline.
paragraphs.translationZh: (5) 当我们沉入海浪的背面时，我跳上防水布，并将其向船尾展开，靠近理查德·帕克。如果他抗议，我也听不到。我比缝纫机缝纫一块布还快，把船两侧的防水布都挂了下来。我们又开始攀登了。船平稳地向上倾斜。我很难保持平衡。救生艇现在已经盖好，防水布也用板条固定，除了我这边。我挤进边凳和防水布之间，把剩下的防水布拉到头上。我没有太多空间。长凳和船边边缘之间有十二英寸，而侧边的长凳只有一英尺半宽。但即使是在死亡面前，我也没有那么鲁莽地走到船的地板上。还剩下四个钩子可以钩住。我把手伸进开口，拉动绳子。每完成一个钩子，获得下一个钩子就变得越来越困难。我成功了两个。还剩两个钩子。小船平稳而不间断地向上冲去。坡度超过三十度。我能感觉到自己被拉向船尾。我拼命一扭手，成功地用绳子又钩住了一个钩子。这是我能做的最好的了。这项工作不应该从救生艇内部完成，而是从外部完成。我用力拉绳子，因为抓住绳子可以防止我从船的长度上滑下来，这让事情变得更容易。船很快就通过了一个四十五度的斜坡。

paragraphs.sourceText: (6) We must have been at a sixty-degree incline when we reached the summit of the swell and broke through its crest onto the other side. The smallest portion of the swell’s supply of water crashed down on us. I felt as if I were being pummelled (反复猛击) by a great fist. The lifeboat abruptly tilted forward and everything was reversed: I was now at the lower end of the lifeboat, and the water that had swamped it, with a tiger soaking in it, came my way. I did not feel the tiger — I had no precise idea of where Richard Parker was; it was pitch-black beneath the tarpaulin — but before we reached the next valley I was half-drowned.
paragraphs.translationZh: (6) 当我们到达浪尖并突破浪尖到达另一边时，我们一定处于六十度的倾斜状态。涌浪中最小的一部分水流冲到了我们身上。我感觉自己好像被一只巨拳猛击。救生艇突然向前倾斜，一切都颠倒过来了：我现在在救生艇的下端，淹没救生艇的水，一只浸泡在里面的老虎，向我袭来。我没有感觉到老虎——我不知道理查德·帕克在哪里；我没有感觉到老虎的存在。防水布下面一片漆黑——但在我们到达下一个山谷之前，我已经被淹了一半。

paragraphs.sourceText: (7) For the rest of that day and into the night, we went up and down, up and down, up and down, until terror became monotonous and was replaced by numbness and a complete giving-up. I held on to the tarpaulin rope with one hand and the edge of the bow bench with the other, while my body lay flat against the side bench. In this position — water pouring in, water pouring out — the tarpaulin beat me to a pulp, I was soaked and chilled, and I was bruised and cut by bones and turtle shells. The noise of the storm was constant, as was Richard Parker’s snarling.
paragraphs.translationZh: (7) 那天剩下的时间和夜晚，我们上上下下，上上下下，上上下下，直到恐惧变得单调，取而代之的是麻木和彻底的放弃。我一手抓住油布绳，一手抓住船头凳的边缘，身体平躺在边凳上。在这个姿势——水涌进来，水涌出来——防水布把我打得稀烂，我浑身湿透，冰冷，身上还被骨头和龟壳擦伤、割伤。暴风雨的噪音持续不断，理查德·帕克的咆哮声也是如此。

paragraphs.sourceText: (8) Sometime during the night my mind noted that the storm was over. We were bobbing on the sea in a normal way. Through a tear in the tarpaulin I glimpsed the night sky. Starry and cloudless. I undid the tarpaulin and lay on top of it.
paragraphs.translationZh: (8) 夜里的某个时候，我的大脑注意到暴风雨已经结束了。我们以正常的方式在海上漂浮。透过防水布的裂口，我瞥见了夜空。繁星点点，万里无云。我解开防水布并躺在上面。

paragraphs.sourceText: What is humility associated with?
paragraphs.translationZh: 谦卑与什么相关？

paragraphs.sourceText: Humility is considered by many philosophers a core element of virtue, which has important benefits to the individual and society. Humility is associated with avoiding conflict, fostering reconciliation, acceptance, and peaceful coexistence. We generally perceive humility as a positive trait, and even feel naturally drawn to humble individuals.
paragraphs.translationZh: 许多哲学家认为谦逊是美德的核心要素，对个人和社会都有重要的好处。谦逊与避免冲突、促进和解、接受以及和平共处有关。我们通常认为谦逊是一种积极的品质，甚至自然而然地会被谦虚的人所吸引。

paragraphs.sourceText: Humility is also associated with personal happiness. Humble people generally have a great appreciation for living and for day-to-day experiences, and they are often family- and relationship-oriented. The call for humility is likely grounded in the observation that humility is associated with appreciation of life and interpersonal relationships. Living a simple life and being down-to-earth not only give you a good social life. They also help you earn the respect of other people. Humble people would avoid giving themselves praise as much as they can. Appreciation and recognition of their abilities normally come from other people. As the saying goes, respect is earned and not demanded. When people start taking notice of your good qualities without your asking for it, humility has done its job.
paragraphs.translationZh: 谦虚也与个人幸福有关。谦虚的人通常非常欣赏生活和日常经历，并且通常以家庭和人际关系为导向。对谦逊的呼吁可能是基于这样的观察：谦逊与对生活和人际关系的欣赏有关。过着简单的生活，脚踏实地，不仅可以给你带来良好的社交生活。他们还可以帮助您赢得其他人的尊重。谦虚的人会尽可能避免自我赞扬。对他们能力的欣赏和认可通常来自其他人。俗话说，尊重是赢得的，而不是索取的。当人们在你不主动要求的情况下开始注意到你的优点时，谦逊就发挥了作用。

paragraphs.sourceText: Humility and ambition
paragraphs.translationZh: 谦虚和野心

paragraphs.sourceText: There has been a remarkable conflict between the call for humility and the societal value system that rewards competitiveness and prominence. General wisdom is that it’s harder to advance our career when we humbly stand back instead of promoting ourselves. Humility is frequently perceived as a weakness. Therefore, we tend to spend most of our lives working to achieve the opposite of humility — we strive for recognition. We don’t want to be like others — we want to be better. There is barely a moment in our lives when we are not confronted with some kind of yearning or need. Of course, many of these fulfill basic functions and thus are necessary to sustain life, e.g., craving to eat, drink, rest, and comfort. They may temporarily preoccupy our minds but may otherwise not represent a major distraction. Yet in excess, desire can consume our minds and may blind us to the fortune of our existence. We all know individuals who seem obsessively driven by some form of craving, e.g., wealth, beauty, and status. Their mind tells them that these things will make them feel fulfilled, and they won’t rest until they achieve their goals. In our busy lives, we usually feel there’s something we “should be” accomplishing. Many of these may be indeed necessary to support our lives, but many may not.
paragraphs.translationZh: 对谦逊的呼唤与奖励竞争力和显赫地位的社会价值体系之间存在着显着的冲突。一般的观点是，当我们谦虚地退缩而不是提升自己时，我们的职业生涯就更难发展。谦虚常常被视为一种弱点。因此，我们倾向于花费一生的大部分时间来实现与谦逊相反的目标——我们努力获得认可。我们不想和别人一样——我们想变得更好。在我们的生活中，几乎每时每刻我们都会遇到某种渴望或需要。当然，其中许多满足基本功能，因此是维持生命所必需的，例如渴望吃、喝、休息和舒适。它们可能会暂时吸引我们的注意力，但在其他方面可能不会造成主要的干扰。然而，过度的欲望会消耗我们的思想，并使我们对自己存在的命运视而不见。我们都知道有些人似乎被某种形式的渴望所驱动，例如财富、美丽和地位。他们的大脑告诉他们，这些事情会让他们感到满足，并且不实现目标他们不会休息。在忙碌的生活中，我们通常会觉得有些事情是我们“应该”完成的。其中许多可能确实是维持我们生活所必需的，但也有许多可能不是。

paragraphs.sourceText: Can we be humble and ambitious? Yes, we can, but only if we compromise on both ends. In the end, it’s our decision — it’s up to us to choose wisely.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们能谦虚而雄心勃勃吗？是的，我们可以，但前提是我们在两端都做出妥协。最终，这是我们的决定——由我们做出明智的选择。

paragraphs.sourceText: Culture is a dynamic force for change rather than a rigid set of forms or parameters that must be strictly adhered. As the World Commission on Culture (1) _______ and Development noted, a society’s culture in neither static or unchanging but (2) _______ rather is in a constant state of flux, is influencing and influenced by other (3) _______ world-views and expressive forms. The current era of globalization is taking a (4) _______ homogenizing influence on local culture. Since this phenomenon promotes the (5) _______ integration of societies and has provided millions of people with new opportunities, it may also bring with it a loss of uniqueness of local culture. This is specially true for traditional societies and communities, which are (6) _______ exposed to rapid “modernization” based on models imported from outside and not adapted to its context. (7) _______

Balancing the benefits of integrating into a globalized world against protecting the uniqueness of local culture requires the careful approach. Placing (8) _______ culture at the heart of development policies does not mean to confine and fix it in a conservative way, but in the contrary to invest in the potential of (9) _______ sustainable progress. Respect for the diversity of cultures also create the (10)_______ conditions for mutual understanding, dialogue and peace.
Language as communication
paragraphs.translationZh: 语言作为交流

paragraphs.sourceText: Perhaps the most fundamental reality of language learning is that language is a tool for communication. As obviously as this point may seem, its (1) implications are not always clear to students as they should be. Remember that (2) many students’ experience of English learning trains them to see English as nothing but a communication tool. The daily reality of English study for many (3) students is one of memorizing words and rules in preparation for a test and rarely involves in using English for communicative purposes. After years of this (4) kind of study, students come to see language learning as an exercise that is primarily geared to formal accuracy, specially on tests. Such non- (5) communicative approaches to English study tend to focus students’ attention on form to the exclusion of use.
paragraphs.translationZh: 也许语言学习最基本的现实是语言是交流的工具。尽管这一点看起来很明显，但学生们并不总是清楚其（1）的含义。请记住，（2）许多学生的英语学习经历训练他们将英语视为一种交流工具。对于许多（3）名学生来说，日常英语学习的现实是记住单词和规则以准备考试，很少涉及使用英语进行交流。经过多年的这种（4）类型的学习，学生开始将语言学习视为一种主要针对形式准确性的练习，特别是在测试中。这种非（5）交际英语学习方法往往会将学生的注意力集中在形式上而忽视了使用。

paragraphs.sourceText: The study of English is potentially more appealed when English is (6) presented as a key for establishing communication with a new world. This communication can take a variety of forms, it can mean sharing ideas face to (7) face with someone from a foreign country or gaining an access to the (8) knowledge embedded in the world’s vast library of materials published in English. In either cases, learning English means developing the ability to (9) understand and interact with a universe that is largely inaccessible for those who (10) don’t know English.
paragraphs.translationZh: 当英语被 (6) 视为与新世界建立沟通的关键时，英语研究可能会更有吸引力。这种交流可以采取多种形式，它可以意味着与来自外国的人面对面地分享想法（7），或者获得嵌入在世界上以英语出版的庞大资料库中的知识（8）。无论哪种情况，学习英语都意味着培养（9）理解宇宙并与之互动的能力，而对于那些（10）不懂英语的人来说，这在很大程度上是无法进入的。
